'''Vivien Kirk''' is a New Zealand mathematician who studies [[dynamical system]]s. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Auckland]], where she also serves as associate pro-vice chancellor graduate research,{{r|profile}} and was president of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]] for 2017–2019.{{r|pres}}

==Education and career==
After earning bachelor's and master's degrees at the University of Auckland, Kirk went to the [[University of Cambridge]] for doctoral studies.{{r|profile}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1990; her dissertation, ''Destruction of tori in dissipative flows'', was supervised by [[Nigel Weiss]].{{r|mgp}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and at the [[California Institute of Technology]].{{r|profile}} Kirk's notable students include [[Alona Ben-Tal]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=A Study of Symmetric Forced Oscillators |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/2323 |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland |date=2001 |degree=Doctoral |language=en |first=Alona |last=Ben-Tal}}</ref>

==Books==
Kirk is the co-author of the books ''Mathematical Analysis of Complex Cellular Activity'' (Springer, 2015) and ''Models of Calcium Signalling'' (Springer, 2016).

==Recognition==
In 2017, Kirk won the [[Miriam Dell]] Excellence in Science Mentoring Award of New Zealand's Association for Women in the Sciences, in part for her efforts in founding and running a series of annual workshops for young women in mathematics and physics since 2007.{{r|dell}}
